screening.reason: Inclusion 2-3: a tutorial paper that performs an original ASD vs TD classification analysis on ABIDE rs-fMRI connectivity data, comparing six classifiers and explicitly demonstrating cross-validation/leakage pitfalls.

evidence_spans.text:
The inputs to the classification pipeline 
are the 77 ASD and 77 TD connectivity matrices (hence 154 data 
samples in total), where each connectivity matrix consists of 
19,900 features.
evidence_spans.claim: 154 ABIDE subjects (77 ASD, 77 TD) with 19,900 connectivity features (200x200 Craddock-atlas matrix) were used.

evidence_spans.text:

evidence_spans.claim: Data were balanced per site (equal ASD/TD counts) and matched on IQ, age and head movement.

evidence_spans.claim: 200 ROIs were derived from the Craddock atlas to compute connectivity matrices.

evidence_spans.text:
Data presented in this study underwent standard fMRI pre-
processing (i.e., realignment, normalization, and smoothing) 
implemented in SPM12b. Data were preprocessed according to 
standard SPM protocols including realignment, normalization 
to a study specific template using DARTEL, smoothing, band-
pass filtering (0.01–0.05 Hz), and scrubbing to account for head 
movements (63).
evidence_spans.claim: Data were preprocessed with SPM12 (realignment, DARTEL normalization, smoothing, band-pass filtering, motion scrubbing).

evidence_spans.text:
The performance of each classifier is assessed by nested cross-
validation: 10-folds are used in the outer cross-validation loop for 
the performance estimation, and 10-folds are used in the inner 
cross-validation loop to determine the optimal threshold value 
t for feature selection, or the optimal regularization parameter 
for lasso-regularized
evidence_spans.claim: Nested 10x10-fold cross-validation was used: outer loop for performance estimation, inner loop for feature-selection/tuning-parameter selection.

evidence_spans.text:
One pitfall is given when feature 
selection or selection of tuning parameters is performed on the full 
data, i.e., on data samples from both the training and the test set.
evidence_spans.claim: The paper explicitly identifies the 'peeking'/double-dipping pitfall of performing feature selection on the full dataset rather than training data only.

evidence_spans.text:
If, however, we use the entire dataset to select the 
features with a mean difference above a threshold value t = 0.10, 
classification with a linear SVM yields a test accuracy of 91%. If 
the feature selection is correctly applied using only the training

evidence_spans.claim: A simulation shows that incorrect (whole-dataset) feature selection can inflate accuracy to 91% versus 45-56% when feature selection is correctly confined to the training set.

evidence_spans.text:
We took the so far best performing classifier – the support 
vector machine – and applied it to the data set after this stand-

evidence_spans.claim: Per-site z-standardization (train-only mean/SD) improved the best classifier's (SVM) accuracy from 63% to 68%.

evidence_spans.text:
Another possibility to assess the generalizability of the clas-
sifier to data from different sites is to form training and test sets 
from different sites. An example of this approach is leave-one-
site-out cross-validation, where the test set contains data from a 
site that has not been used in the training set (36).
evidence_spans.claim: Leave-one-site-out cross-validation is described as an approach to assess generalizability across sites.

assessments.support: N (77 ASD, 77 TD) and per-site balancing/matching on IQ, age and head movement are explicitly reported.
SPM12/DARTEL preprocessing pipeline and the 200-ROI Craddock atlas are explicitly described.
ASD/TD labels are taken from the ABIDE repository; the diagnostic-instrument source is not independently restated in the main text.

The paper explicitly uses nested 10x10 cross-validation to avoid optimistic bias, demonstrates via simulation the magnitude of the 'peeking' leakage problem, and describes train-only standardization to avoid double-dipping — an explicit positive example of leakage control.

risk_of_bias.summary: A methodologically rigorous tutorial that both applies and explicitly teaches leakage-avoidance (nested CV, train-only standardization) on a real ABIDE classification pipeline; main residual gap is that the diagnosis-source instrument is not independently restated.

charting.title: Promises, Pitfalls, and Basic Guidelines for Applying Machine Learning Classifiers to Psychiatric Imaging Data, with Autism as an Example
charting.primary_focus: Diagnosis / methodological tutorial on ML classification pitfalls
charting.primary_goal: Demonstrate and compare ML classification pipelines for ASD vs TD using ABIDE RS-fMRI data, while teaching methodological pitfalls (peeking/double-dipping, site effects)
charting.dataset_openly_available: MATLAB code for all pipelines publicly available (ETH website)
charting.specific_features: 200x200 Craddock-atlas ROI-to-ROI Pearson correlation matrix (19,900 features)
charting.feature_extraction_tools: SPM12 (realignment, DARTEL normalization, smoothing, band-pass filter 0.01-0.05Hz, motion scrubbing)
charting.importance_method: Mean-difference threshold feature selection (t-value threshold), with nested CV for threshold tuning
charting.specific_algorithms: Logistic regression, lasso-regularized logistic regression, linear SVM, probabilistic neural network, linear discriminant analysis, Gaussian naive Bayes
charting.validation_methodology: Nested 10x10-fold cross-validation (outer loop for performance, inner loop for feature-selection/tuning-parameter selection); explicit avoidance of double-dipping via train-only feature selection and standardization
charting.key_performance_results: LR 58%, LassoLR 58%, SVM 63% (best out-of-the-box), PNN 58%, LDA 57%, GNB 61% accuracy; SVM accuracy increased to 68% after per-site (train-only) z-standardization; all classifiers significantly better than chance (p<0.001).
charting.summary_key_findings: Out-of-the-box ML classifiers applied correctly (nested CV) to ABIDE rs-fMRI connectivity achieve about 60-70% accuracy (best: SVM 63%, improving to 68% with site standardization); incorrect feature selection on the full dataset ('peeking'/double-dipping) can spuriously inflate accuracy to 91% in a null simulation, illustrating a major pitfall in the field.
charting.future_directions_recommended: Leave-one-site-out cross-validation and further site-effect correction beyond linear z-transformation; stable feature selection methods for biomarker interpretation.
charting.reviewer_notes: A methods/tutorial paper that nonetheless performs an original classification analysis on real ABIDE data; valuable as a positive worked example of leakage-avoidance practice for the review's CL5 checklist item.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction / methodological tutorial; ABIDE, N=154 (77 ASD, 77 TD), balanced and matched per site.
narrative_row.methods: SPM12/DARTEL-preprocessed rs-fMRI; 200-ROI Craddock-atlas connectivity (19,900 features); six classifiers (LR, LassoLR, SVM, PNN, LDA, GNB) compared via nested 10x10-fold cross-validation with train-only feature selection and standardization.
narrative_row.outcomes: Best out-of-the-box accuracy 63% (linear SVM), improving to 68% with per-site train-only standardization; a simulation shows incorrect whole-dataset feature selection can inflate accuracy to 91%, illustrating the 'peeking'/double-dipping pitfall.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Diagnosis-source instrument not independently restated; leave-one-site-out CV discussed but not reported as the authors' own executed analysis; relatively modest sample size (N=154).
narrative_row.relevance_notes: A rare positive methodological exemplar in this corpus: explicitly demonstrates and guards against the leakage patterns (whole-dataset feature selection/standardization) that affect several other ABIDE predictive papers in this review.

kg_link.finding: Nested-cross-validated classifiers achieve 57-63% accuracy (best: linear SVM 63%, improving to 68% with per-site train-only standardization); a simulation demonstrates that incorrect whole-dataset feature selection can inflate accuracy to 91%, illustrating the 'peeking'/double-dipping pitfall in ABIDE-based ML classification.
